rationale: Coptic numeral 170 (ⲣ=100, ⲓ=10, ⲝ=60) functioning as chapter-number marker bracketing the kephalaion title. Appears three times on this page (lines 7, 9 ×2) as decorative title-boundary indicator. Should be read as a chapter-number sigil rather than as a syntactic word. Documents standard Manichaean Kephalaia codex convention for chapter numbering on opening pages.

Hapax in this corpus. Most plausible analysis: ⲙⲁⲛ-ⲥⲁⲧⲡ̄ 'place of choice/election' (Lyc. ⲍ for ⲛ in compound place-noun prefix ⲙⲁⲛ-, paralleling ⲙⲁⲛⲭⲟⲣⲉ 'stronghold,' ⲙⲁⲛⲣⲁⲓ̈ⲥ 'watch-post,' etc.). Confidence low pending parallels.

Possibly ⲁϯ-ϩⲟⲩⲏⲛⲓⲁ where -ϩⲟⲩⲏⲛⲓⲁ renders Greek εὔνοια 'goodwill, kindly attention' (with Lyc. ⲍ-onset and vowel-adjustment of -ⲉⲩⲛⲟⲓⲁ → -ⲍⲟⲩⲛⲏⲛⲓⲁ → -ϩⲟⲩⲏⲛⲓⲁ). Construction with ⲥⲱⲧⲙ̄ 'hear' + adverbial complement: 'Disciple, listen attentively to (this) saying.' Confidence low.

Compound: ϣⲡⲛ̄ ('suddenly') + ϣⲱⲡⲉ ('happen, become') = 'sudden happening.' Standard Coptic for an unexpected occurrence. Used here in the chapter's structuring contrast: gradual death (ⲱⲥⲕ ⲁⲉⲓ 'delay coming') vs. sudden death (ⲙⲟⲩ ϩⲛ ⲟⲩϣⲡⲛϣⲱⲡⲉ 'die in a sudden event').

ⲕⲉ- ('other, again') + ⲕⲁⲩⲉ ('others'); the doubled-other construction emphasizing successive enumeration: 'yet others (in turn).' Used in the kephalaion's typology where multiple classes of dying souls are distinguished.
